children: TOKYO--Japan recorded its widest trade deficit in seven months in August as higher energy costs inflated the country's import bill.

The trade deficit stood at 1.1056 trillion yen, equivalent to $7.13 billion, last month, according to government data released Wednesday. That compared with a 638.344 billion yen shortfall in July and marked the biggest gap since January.
Although Tokyo's strategy to secure energy via routes bypassing the Strait of Hormuz has helped maintain supply flows, alternative sources carry higher price tags.
Exports rose 19.3% from a year earlier in August, while imports grew 28.0%, the data showed.

Despite rising oil prices, Bank of Japan policymakers believe that the impact of the Middle East conflict is unlikely to cause a significant downturn in the domestic economy. The central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates to 1.25% from 1% at its two-day meeting ending Friday.
